item: the columnar job names tests/test_external_freshness.py, whose two DuckDB-dependent tests passed vacuously in every job
summary: tests/test_external_freshness.py has two tests that depend on duckdb being installed: test_duckdb_version_coupling_holds_when_installed returns early when duckdb is not importable, and test_nothing_is_stale calls the registry's evaluate(), whose track-duckdb-version branch (the duckdb-crypto-extension and duckdb-httpfs-extension entries) reports info instead of comparing versions when duckdb is absent. No job that installs duckdb ran the file, so the check that the installed duckdb meets the registered floor (the coupling the bundled httpfs extension and the storage format depend on) passed vacuously in every job that ran the file (test, Core-only, portability, the urllib3 floor, and the tag-time release run; none installs [columnar]) and never ran against a real duckdb in CI. The columnar job's first pytest step now names the file after the 28 files #1654 listed, so the check runs against the duckdb the job resolves. Measured with scratch installs on the fresh main tip: the 29-file step passes 472 with 2 skips on duckdb 1.5.6 (66.6 s) and 471 with 3 skips on duckdb 2.0.0 (72.7 s); the file adds 15 tests and about 7 s, thirteen of them registry, pin and bundled-data checks that also run in the test job. Stated limits: the ratchet (tests/test_skipped_tests_have_a_ci_job_that_runs_them.py) does not see this file until a test in it becomes an importorskip (Q's follow-on), and test_nothing_is_stale's duckdb branch has no skip to detect, so only keeping the file's name in the step stops that branch going vacuous again; until then dropping the name stays green; the runner's own figure for the added seconds is not measured here.
